Test: Inspect meaningful images, icon-only controls, and decorative images in the accessibility tree. Compare each exposed alternative with the asset's purpose.
For prerecorded audio-only and silent video, locate equivalent text or an applicable audio alternative. Compare it with the entire source.
Play prerecorded synchronized media and compare captions with speech, speaker changes, relevant sounds, and timing.
Play prerecorded video with the display hidden. Verify that an audio-description track or a media alternative conveys relevant visual events.
Join a live media session and verify captions capture speech and meaningful audio during the event.
Play prerecorded synchronized video and verify that meaningful visual information is conveyed in the audio or an audio-description track.
Play prerecorded synchronized media and check that a sign-language version covers the audio information.
Check key visuals in a description track. Where ordinary pauses are too short, verify extended description is available.
Compare a full media alternative with the prerecorded video and check that it conveys relevant audio, visuals, order, and interactions.
Follow live audio-only content alongside its accessible alternative and check that the information is equivalent.
Inspect headings, field labels, groups, lists, and table headers in the DOM and accessibility tree.
Compare visual and programmatic reading order for content whose meaning depends on its sequence.
Read instructions without using visual position, shape, color, or sound as a cue. Verify the referenced action can still be identified.
Rotate a supported device in both directions and verify content and controls work unless one orientation is essential.
Inspect personal-data inputs against the WCAG input-purpose list and verify appropriate autocomplete semantics where supported.
Inspect the programmatic purpose of interface components, icons, and regions in markup.
Disable color cues or view in grayscale. Check links, errors, charts, and selected states for a second identifying cue.
Load a page with autoplay audio. If playback exceeds three seconds, verify a pause, stop, or independent volume control.
Measure actual text against its rendered backgrounds in each state. Check 4.5:1 for regular text and 3:1 for large text, with listed exceptions.
Increase text to 200% and check clipping, overlapping controls, missing content, and lost functionality.
Inspect banners and images containing styled text. Verify that text is rendered as text where the technology supports it, subject to exceptions.
Measure rendered text against its background. Check 7:1 for regular text and 4.5:1 for large text, with listed exceptions.
For eligible speech-first recordings, check for absent, switchable, or sufficiently quiet background audio using the criterion's conditions.
For blocks of text, verify users can control colors and meet line length, alignment, spacing, and resizing conditions.
Inspect informational images of text. Confirm every example qualifies as purely decorative or essential.
Test vertically scrolling content at 320 CSS px wide and horizontally scrolling content at 256 CSS px high. Verify content and usage without two-direction scrolling, subject to exceptions.
Measure visual boundaries, states, and meaningful graphics against adjacent colors. Check 3:1 and record applicable exceptions.
Apply the WCAG line, paragraph, letter, and word spacing overrides together. Check for loss of content or functionality.
Trigger tooltips and popovers using mouse and keyboard. Check dismissal, hover movement into the content, and persistence.
Complete each applicable task using only the keyboard. Record any operation that requires pointer input and evaluate the path-dependent exception.
Enter and exit widgets using the keyboard. Check that any nonstandard exit is communicated.
Complete every function using only the keyboard, including flows involving path-dependent pointer interaction.
Find single-character shortcuts and verify they can be disabled, remapped, or work only when the relevant control has focus.
Trigger each time limit and verify adjustment, deactivation, or extension under the criterion's timing rules. Document exceptions.
Check moving content and auto-updating regions shown alongside other content. Test an applicable stop, pause, hide, or frequency control.
Inventory time-dependent tasks and determine whether each time constraint falls within a listed exception.
Trigger interruptions during a flow and verify users can postpone or suppress them, except emergencies.
Let a session expire while editing. Reauthenticate and check that entered data and the task remain available.
Check inactivity limits that can cause data loss. Verify users are told the duration unless data is preserved for at least 20 hours.
Review flashing content in each relevant viewport. Use threshold analysis where flash frequency exceeds three in any one second.
Check that nothing flashes more than three times during any one-second period.
Trigger motion through user interaction. Verify disablement for motion that is inessential to functionality or information.
Use landmark navigation or a skip mechanism to bypass repeated blocks and reach main content.
Inspect browser titles across routes and verify each identifies the page topic or purpose.
Tab through the interface including menus, dialogs, and return paths. Confirm the sequence preserves meaning and operation.
Read links with their programmatically available surrounding context. Verify that the destination or action can be identified.
Find each applicable page through two mechanisms, such as navigation and search. Check the process-page exception.
Read headings and labels apart from body text and verify they describe each section or control.
Tab through links and controls in each theme and verify an observable keyboard focus indicator.
Verify that users can determine their current location within the site or related page set.
Read links without surrounding context and verify each purpose can be determined, subject to the ambiguity exception.
Review long content and confirm that sections use descriptive headings.
Tab through elements near sticky bars, banners, and dialogs. Check that author-created content never hides the focused component entirely.
Repeat the occlusion test and verify that no part of the focused component is hidden by author-created content.
Measure the keyboard focus indicator against the equivalent two-CSS-pixel perimeter area and the 3:1 state-change contrast rule. Check exceptions.
Test multipoint and path-based gestures using a single pointer without following a path. Document any essential gesture.
Press on a target and release outside it. Verify the action can be avoided, aborted, undone, or reversed as specified.
Compare visible text on each control with its computed accessible name. Try speaking the visible label with voice control.
Try motion-triggered actions using normal controls and verify motion response can be disabled, subject to applicable exceptions.
Measure pointer targets against 44 by 44 CSS px and document any applicable exception.
Switch among supported pointer, keyboard, and other inputs while completing the same task. Check any restrictions against exceptions.
For every drag operation, complete the same task with a single pointer and no dragging. Record essential or user-agent exceptions.
Measure pointer targets against 24 by 24 CSS px. For undersized targets claiming spacing, test the 24 CSS px circle geometry against nearby targets.
Inspect the default document language and verify that screen readers pronounce the primary content using the expected language.
Inspect mixed-language passages for programmatic language changes and review the listed exceptions.
Locate unusual terms, jargon, and idioms. Verify readers can reach an appropriate definition.
Locate abbreviations and verify a mechanism supplies the expansion or meaning.
Evaluate difficult text against the reading-level requirement and verify that an accessible simpler version or supplemental content is provided when required.
Identify words whose meaning depends on pronunciation and verify a user can obtain that pronunciation.
Move focus onto interactive controls without activating them and check for unexpected context changes.
Change values in selects, toggles, and fields. Confirm that automatic context changes are explained before use.
Compare repeated navigation across pages in the same set and verify its relative order is consistent unless the user changes it.
Compare components that perform the same function across pages. Check their visible and programmatic identification.
Trigger flows that cause context changes and verify they occur on request or can be disabled.
Compare the order of repeated help mechanisms across pages at the same presentation size, accounting for user-initiated changes.
Submit invalid data. Verify the affected field and the specific error are identified in text.
Review input controls before submitting. Verify required labels, formats, and other instructions are provided.
Trigger errors with known corrections. Verify helpful suggestions are available unless they undermine security or purpose.
Try a qualifying legal, financial, test, or user-data submission. Check that it can be reversed, corrected after checking, or confirmed before final submission.
Look for context-sensitive guidance near inputs or other tasks that require it.
Try a form that submits information and verify reversal, validation with correction, or review and confirmation.
Repeat information within one process. Verify automatic population or selection of the previous entry, subject to the criterion's exceptions.
Test sign-in, MFA, and recovery. Check cognitive test alternatives or assistance, including paste and password-manager support where applicable.
Test authentication steps requiring memory, transcription, object recognition, or personal content recognition. Verify a qualifying alternative or assistance.
Inspect computed names, roles, values, and states. Change widget state with assistive technology and verify it is reported.
Trigger search results, confirmations, progress, and errors without moving focus. Verify appropriate announcements to assistive technology.
